before:
Captain Marcus Gavin sat staring dumbfounded at the screen on the wall, the large display was an older model, one that had seen its share of mission launches and training exercises, despite all of this it still showed the growing horror in high definition for the entire control room to see. The few personnel left in the room made up about 1% of its capacity. Those left to man the last mission mankind would ever send into the darkness of space Marcus thought.

The first age of man ended much as it had begun with silence.

At the close of the 22nd century, Earth stood empty, bereft of humans, void of their monuments. The beasts once again ruled the planet. The instrument of man's demise, the alien weapon, found beneath the ice of Earth, now stood as the last temple to technology on the small blue world.

Though Earth stood empty of man, the universe did not. Seeing the end coming, humanity, in a last desperate act to save itself, created the ARC.

With the advanced knowledge gleaned from the alien weapon, humankind now could safely enter a frozen state of slumber and awaken centuries later.

The last remnants of humanity, twenty thousand souls in all, slept away the ages, aboard the massive ship as it floated out near mars until it was safe to step foot upon the globe once again.

The grand ARC, man's best hope for a future, eventually returned to the little blue planet, the last evidence of man's mastery over the machine, stood sentry over the small blue world.

The ship's artificial intelligence watched and waited, the machine standing vigil, analyzing, and scanning the world man once called home. Only once the world was again deemed safe were the PODS release back to the now-feral world, the slumbering inheritors of man's destiny.

Frozen in the small pods, they would rocket back to the planet, allowing man once again to take their rightful place upon the Earth.

However, some did not return. Either by accident or some purpose not understood by man or machine, they floated above the planet, locked in orbit, locked in sleep, randomly falling to the world as the age's past.

Those who paid attention to such things called them fallen, here is the story of one lost soul, robbed of his world and returned to an earth which has regressed to a time long before his own.
after:
Captain Marcus Gavin stared at the screen on the control-room wall. The aging display had served through years of training exercises and mission launches. Now it showed the end of his world in high definition.

Only a handful of personnel remained at their stations. They would send humanity’s last mission into space.

At the close of the twenty-second century, the First Age of Man ended in silence. The alien weapon found beneath Earth’s ice had become the instrument of humanity’s destruction.

But not its extinction.

Scientists had learned enough from the weapon to place a human being in frozen slumber and wake them centuries later. With that knowledge, humanity built the ARC. Twenty thousand people slept aboard the great ship as it waited near Mars for Earth to become habitable again.

Eventually, the ARC returned. Its artificial intelligence kept watch over the planet, scanning the world its passengers had once called home. When conditions were safe, it began releasing the pods.

The sleepers fell back to Earth to reclaim a world that had gone on without them.

Some pods did not descend. Whether by accident or by a purpose neither humanity nor its machines understood, they remained in orbit. The centuries passed. One by one, the stragglers fell.

Those who watched the skies called them the fallen.

Marcus Gavin was one of them.

before:
When the old world ended, it did not go gently.

Humanity’s First Age choked on ash, radiation, and the shattering of tectonic plates. In those final, desperate years before the sky turned black, the architect engineers of the ARC Project buried the remnants of civilization beneath miles of granite and basalt. Deep within subterranean stasis crypts, thousands of souls were sealed into cryo-pods, programmed to sleep until the planetary atmosphere healed and the surface became hospitable once more.

They were meant to wake together. They were meant to rebuild a technological paradise.

They awoke to a nightmare.

Over centuries of dormancy, the earth did not heal in the manner the ancient scientists had predicted. Deep within the fractured mantle, alien mineral formations—towering crystals of obsidian, sapphire, and radiant emerald—sprouted like malignant forests across mountain ranges and desolate plains. The crystals did not merely glow; they bled energy. They warped the fundamental laws of physics, bleeding an exotic quantum resonance into the soil, the water, and the air.

This was the Source.

When the sleepers finally began to awaken, their pods did not open in unison. Clock cycles failed; geothermal circuits degraded; tectonic shifts crushed entire vaults. Sleepers tumbled out into the blinding daylight scattered across centuries. Those who emerged into the Second Age found an untamed, feudal frontier populated by the descendants of surface survivors and the ancient, arboreal Silvan clans.

And the crystals changed them.

Those born near the crystal fissures found themselves attuned to the energy. They could manipulate heat, density, and kinetic force with a thought. They became the Gifted—Source Mages. Around this strange new power arose the Church of Aurtus, a monastic order built upon the Four Tenets: Life, Order, Balance, and Memory. To safeguard the realm from rogue mages, the Order of the Wardens was established—elite adjudicators armed with rune-forged blades who traveled the frontiers dispensing justice and keeping the delicate peace between human settlements and the wild lands.

Yet the greatest threat to the Second Age did not come from the wild. It came from the East.

Decades before the others, an ARC sleeper of immense intellect and terrifying ambition had awakened in the eastern wastes. Where others saw the crystals as sacred or perilous, she saw them as raw material for absolute dominion. Imbuing her own biology with black crystal resonance, she declared herself Empress—the Black Queen.

From her towering obsidian citadel, the Empress built an empire of iron and flesh. Her alchemists harvested the blue crystal resin, forging terrifying cannons that spat liquid fire capable of vaporizing stone battlements. Her flesh-weavers bred twisted abominations—the Chimera—hybrid beasts engineered for battlefield slaughter. And at her right hand stood Lord Seer Juric Rogan, a zealot who enforced her will with cold, telekinetic brutality.

Then, Captain Marcus Gavin awoke.

Crash-landing in the rugged northern frontier, Marcus emerged from his pod with no memory of his past, carrying only the instinct of a soldier and the raw, uncorrupted genetics of the First Age. Taken in by Orah, a gentle farm woman in a secluded mountain valley, Marcus struggled to comprehend this brutal, beautiful new world. But peace was a luxury the Second Age could not afford.

The Empress’s scouts detected the energy signature of Marcus’s crash. Realizing that an uncorrupted ARC survivor carried the genetic key to unlocking ancient military vaults and mastering Source synthesis, the Empress dispatched Chancellor Rogan and her vanguard to hunt him down.

The clash at the mountain outpost was swift and devastating. The Empress’s resin cannons pulverized the old defenses. Though the Wardens—led by the fierce Lorin Corliss and Grand Adjudicator Uri—fought valiantly to protect the frontier, the outpost fell. Corliss and the surviving Wardens were forced to retreat toward the Barrens, while Marcus was driven into the wilderness with a spectral companion, hunted by an empire that would stop at nothing to claim his blood.

Now, the drums of war echo across the continent. 

In the high halls of the eastern capital, Lord Seer Rogan ascends the throne of judgment, ready to crush all who dare defy the Empress. In the shadowed keeps of the Church, the fanatic inquisitors of the Sword of the Faithful sharpen their silver blades. And in the deep woods of Silvan, Marcus Gavin must decide whether to keep running from his destiny... or stand and break the Black Queen's throne.
after:
The ARC had carried twenty thousand sleepers away from a dying Earth. When its machines judged the planet safe, the ship released its passengers in pods. Some returned long after the others, waking to a world they could scarcely recognize.

Captain Marcus Gavin had been an engineer. He had built irrigation systems in the deserts of Africa; his combat training belonged to a life he could barely reach. On this changed Earth, those memories offered little protection.

Orah gave him a home. For a time, he believed he could keep it.

Her death ended that hope. The power Marcus unleashed against her killers left him alive, but it could not restore what he had lost. With Maelen’s help, he began to learn what it meant to be a mage—and what the Empress demanded of those who possessed the gift.

Others were learning the cost of her rule. The Wardens were scattered. The Church was under attack. Even the mages could not agree whether to resist or submit. Nero had seen creatures wield magic against the helpless, and each fresh atrocity hardened his judgment of everyone who shared their power.

In the north, the survivors sought allies. In the occupied lands, Rogan enforced the Empress’s will.

Marcus had survived his return to Earth. Survival would no longer be enough.

before:
The Second Age of Man had arrived in fire.

Centuries after the First Age choked beneath nuclear ash and tectonic ruin, the subterranean stasis vaults of the ARC Project had finally cracked. But humanity did not emerge into a healed world of machines and light. They awoke into a fractured, wild frontier where the earth itself had changed. Primal alien crystals had erupted through the scarred crust, bleeding an exotic, living energy known as the Source into every living thing.

Some men became Gifted, mastering kinetic force and crystal flame. The Church of Aurtus arose to shepherd the survivors under the Four Tenets—Life, Order, Balance, and Memory—while the Order of the Wardens patrolled the wilderness with rune-forged steel, keeping the fragile peace between human enclaves and the proud, ancient Silvan tree kingdoms.

Yet in the east, an older darkness had taken root.

An ARC scientist who had awakened generations before the others cast aside her humanity. Imbuing her body with the resonance of the black crystals, she forged herself into an immortal sovereign: the Empress—the Black Queen. From her towering obsidian citadel, she engineered nightmare armies: altered Chimera beasts that stalked the night, telekinetic Chosen bound to her will, and devastating resin siege cannons that spat liquid blue crystal-fire.

When Captain Marcus Gavin’s stasis pod plummeted to earth in the northern frontier, he brought with him the purest, uncorrupted genetics of the First Age. To the Empress, Marcus was the final missing element: the key to synthesizing an invincible army and mastering the pre-collapse military vaults buried in the mantle.

She unleashed Chancellor Juric Rogan to hunt him down.

The war began with the destruction of the mountain outposts. The Empress’s resin cannons shattered ancient walls, scattering the Wardens and driving Marcus and his spectral companion into the deep forests. Yet as Rogan’s subjugation legions marched across the provinces, the balance of power began to fracture from within.

Along the battered eastern seaboard, Messenger Veric Nero survived the massacre of the shore towns, arriving battered and hollow-eyed with Korlin, his faith turning from humble peace toward an unyielding, burning fanaticism that would birth the Sword of the Faithful. In the north, High Warden Lorin Corliss and Grand Adjudicator Uri joined forces with General Erod Durass and the Silvan canopy warriors, fortifying the squat ramparts of the northern abbey against the coming deluge.

And in the secret groves of the Silvan masters, Marcus Gavin submitted to ancient runic grafting, transforming from a lost relic of the past into something the Second Age had not seen in a thousand years: a Runic Mage of the Source.

The lines have been drawn. Empires crumble not from the strength of their enemies, but from the weight of their own tyranny. 

The siege has begun. The dragon awakens. The empire must fall.
after:
The Empress had broken the agreement.

Across the realm, the institutions that had held an uneasy peace were faltering. The Wardens were scattered, the Church was under attack, and the mages were divided over whether to serve the crown or oppose it.

Marcus Gavin had returned to Earth from the ARC, a sleeper from the First Age. He had hoped to make a life in the world that replaced his own. Instead, he had lost Orah and discovered a power he was still learning to control.

He and Maelen had helped a town resist the Empress’s servants. The victory offered shelter, but the missives waiting for them carried news of a wider war.

Elsewhere, Nero and his companion had survived the slaughter at the shore. They walked inland looking for sanctuary, carrying questions neither the Church nor the crown had answered.

In the north, the Wardens sought help beyond the borders they had once defended.

Resistance was still possible. Whether its survivors could trust one another remained to be seen.

before:
The two men dirty and disheveled entered the small town and slowly made their way in the dead of night towards the stone building of the keep.

It had been nearly eight days since they had come ashore walking the thirty miles to this small hamlet on the outskirts of Vicor.

Nero was exhausted, his mind still reeling over the events at the small shore town, and with the death of Jorun, the old man had sacrificed himself to save the two of them, only to be massacred before their very eyes.

What was happening he wondered, what were these creatures and how was the crown involved.

These questions and more had spun around in his brain since they stepped off the boat onto dry land.
after:
The two men entered the town after dark, their clothes filthy from eight days on the road. Ahead, beyond the common, stood the stone keep.

They had walked thirty miles since coming ashore. Nero could scarcely put one foot before the other, but exhaustion had not dulled the memory of Jorun’s death. The old man had sacrificed himself to save them.

What were those creatures? How was the crown involved?

The questions had followed Nero every mile.

The four men having taken food to feed their families and then taken it to them during the time they were supposed to be working the fields for the Empress. The Lord Seer had instituted rationing despite the commoners' complaints of starvation to ensure he could send more food stock to the troops, he would not tolerate the whining and complaining of the common people whose only reason for existing was to serve him and by serving him, the Empress. after:
Lord Seer Rogan sat upon the throne of judgment, the deep purple robes of his office wrapped around his shoulders like armor. Four men knelt before him.

“You are charged with stealing the Lord Seer’s food and abandoning your posts. How do you plead?” Loric read from the parchment in his hand.

The men had taken food to their families when they should have been working the Empress’s fields. Rogan had imposed rationing to supply the troops. The commoners complained of starvation, but he would not tolerate theft. Their duty was to serve him, and through him, the Empress.

They should be grateful he allowed them to eat at all.

“Pathetic,” he said. “How dare you steal from me?”

None of the men met his eyes.
